title: The Doctrine of the Holy Crown and Unwritten Constitutionalism

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Unlike post-revolutionary France or the United States, Hungary had no single codified constitution until 1949. Instead, like Great Britain, it operated under a *történeti alkotmány* (Historic Constitution) composed of fundamental statutes and centuries of customary law (*szokásjog*).

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Central to this system was the *Szent Korona-tan*: the Holy Crown was more than an object: in the doctrine, as developed by later legal scholarship, it stood for the state, and the king and the nobility were its members (*a korona tagjai*).
